about: Context for translators - not read by the server. `groups`: where the keys under a prefix appear (the longest matching prefix wins). `keys`: a note for one key. `vars`: what each {placeholder} holds; `key_vars` overrides it for one key. scripts/lib/i18n-catalogue.mjs merges this into filex-catalogue-context.json, and web/tests/i18n/langPackCatalogue.test.ts fails when a server key has no group or a placeholder no description.

Why a notification event can never happen on this server, shown greyed beside its switch (Settings → Notifications, Admin → Webhooks) to the administrator who could switch it on. One short sentence; a screen name in brackets (Protection) is the admin page where it is turned on.
The desktop app's folder sync: what the sync engine (the filex program the app runs) reports, shown under each synced folder in the app's Settings and, for a program, in `filex sync run --json`. Short status lines; a sentence ending without a full stop is a status, like the others under the folder. `{seconds}` is the interval of the safety-net check (30 in the app).
groups.server.perm.blocked_extension: API refusal when the person's role blocks a file type they tried to upload, create or rename to. One sentence.
groups.server.perm.app_denied: API refusal when a person lacks one of an app's own permissions (the role editor lists them under the app's name). {permission} is the app's label for it, e.g. “Request signatures”; {app} is the app's name, e.g. “Sign”. One sentence.
API refusal shown when a person lacks a permission (a toast or dialog in the file manager, or an error an API client logs). One sentence; the {action} is a lowercase phrase from server.perm.action.*. Which sentence is said names where the “no” came from: base - the person's built-in role (User, Viewer) does not include it; override - an administrator set an exception for this person alone; role - only administrators ever hold it; rule - the person's custom role {rule} does not include it; role_off - the person's custom role {rule} is switched off; viewer_ceiling - a read-only account can never hold it.
A lowercase verb phrase naming what one permission allows, slotted into the server.perm.denied.* sentences as {action}. Grammar must fit every one of those sentences. Where one verb form cannot fit them all, make {action} a noun phrase and word the sentences around it: Turkish writes “dosya silme” (deleting files) and “Hesabınızın {action} izni yok” (your account has no {action} permission); “override” puts it in quotes as the permission's name.
Email filex sends. Plain text: one line per key, no markup. Written in the RECIPIENT's language as each flow decides it (below).
groups.server.mail.greeting: Email: the first line of every mail filex writes to a person.
groups.server.mail.valid_days: Email (share link, file request): how long the link works.
groups.server.mail.no_expiry: Email (share link, file request): the link has no end date.
Email (share link, file request): a fact line under the introduction - the item, its size, the PIN.
Email: a download link somebody sent from the Share dialog ("Send by email"), or the link an invite falls back to for an address with no account. In the SENDER's language (the one their screen is in).
Email: a file-request (upload) link somebody sent from the Share dialog - the recipient is asked to upload files. In the sender's language.
Email: an existing account was given access to a file or folder (Permissions panel → Invite). In the recipient's account language.
Email: an administrator created an account for the recipient while inviting them; it carries a temporary password. In the language the inviting administrator's screen is in (the new account starts in it too).
The email of a notification digest, to a person who asked to be told by email (a file request's owner, today): the kinds they did not mark urgent were held, and this one email tells what changed, folder by folder, in their account language. The subject is also the digest's stored title.
Email AND notification to the owner of a folder when somebody uploads files through its file-request link. In the folder owner's account language. The subject is also the notification's stored title.
Email: the administrator's "Send test" in the mail settings. In that administrator's language.
The Share dialog, under the "Send by email" box: what happened to the mail the person just sent with a link (sent, partly sent, refused). One short sentence each, in the sender's language; pin_withheld follows a sent/partial sentence when the link has a PIN, which the mail never carries.
Email (filex cloud sign-up only): the verification token for a new tenant. In the visitor's browser language.
groups.server.mail.app_footer: Email: the line filex adds under every mail an installed app sends (a signature request, a reminder…). In the language the app wrote the mail in.
The first line of NOT.txt, the note filex writes beside files uploaded through a file-request link (the uploader's own note follows). Read by the folder's owner, in their language.
API refusal on the platform operator's switch that turns encryption on or off for one tenant (Admin panel → Encryption → Tenants, or an API client). One or two sentences. The last part of the key says why: single_tenant - this server is not multi-tenant, so it has no tenant ceiling to switch, and who may encrypt is set by the encryption policy alone.
API refusal when someone tries to create an end-to-end encrypted folder or file (its key file .filex-e2e.json, or a .fxe) and the encryption rules say no - a toast or dialog in the file manager, or an error an API client logs. One sentence. The last part of the key says why: tenant_disabled - the platform operator has switched encryption off for this organization; policy_off - an administrator has turned encryption off; admins_only - only administrators may create encrypted items; permission - the person's role does not include the Encrypt permission here; approval_required - the policy asks for an administrator's approval first, and the person has none for this folder.
A vault (encryption level 3: one folder whose files, folders and names the server never sees) refuses a request - an API client's log, or a message the file manager shows. One sentence, sometimes two. The key's last part says why: disabled - this server does not offer vaults; not_a_vault - the folder is not a vault; exists - something is already where a new vault was to be made; nested - a vault cannot go inside another encrypted folder; locked - somebody else holds the vault's write lock, and the sentence names them; lock_lost.* - this session no longer holds the write lock (broken: somebody ended it; expired: the connection was lost; idle: nothing was written for the person's idle time; released: the session gave it up; taken: somebody else holds it now); bad_object - an uploaded pack or index file is malformed; pack_exists - a pack with that id is already stored; generation - only the next generation can be committed; keep - the three newest generations are never deleted; keyfile - the vault's key file must keep its vault fields and cannot be removed on its own; path - nothing but the vault writes inside a vault folder; bad_request - the request is malformed; idle_range - the idle-time setting is 1 to 10 minutes; timeout - the server gave up an index write after 60 seconds; break_denied - only the folder's owner or an administrator may end another person's write lock; busy - the lock's record changed under every attempt to update it, try again. Keep 'vault', 'pack', 'index' and 'generation' as the file manager's own words for them.
A refusal or a failed job, said to the person who asked: the file manager, the admin panel, the desktop app, the command line and an AI agent all show this sentence as it is (the API answers it in `message` beside a stable code in `error`). One or two sentences: what happened and, where it applies, what to do. The key's last part is the code: read_only - the storage takes no writes; quota_exceeded - the owner's quota is full; name_taken - something already has the name; locked - an app holds the file; reserved_name - the name is one filex keeps for itself; not_cancellable / finished - a queued job cannot be stopped / is over; timeout, out_of_memory, crashed, app_removed, action_removed, engine_missing, office_unconfigured - why an app's job failed (the _admin forms are shown to an administrator, who can fix it); the e2e request codes (kind_mismatch, not_requestable, path_missing, too_many_pending) - an encryption request that no longer fits the folder.
Plugins → Apps → install review and the app's page: what one permission lets the app do. The administrator reads this before trusting the app with their files. Starts with a verb, no final full stop.
The pages a share or file-request link opens in a browser without JavaScript (and a few in any browser: the error pages, the PIN gate, the "preparing your download" page). In the visitor's browser language. Plain text - the page escapes it.
groups.server.public.pin_: Public page: the PIN gate in front of a protected share or file-request link.
groups.server.public.app_: Public page: an app's link (e.g. a signature request) opened without JavaScript - it lists the files the app shared.
groups.server.public.unlocked_: Public page: shown for a moment after a correct PIN, while the download starts.
groups.server.public.zip_: Public page: a shared folder is being packed into a ZIP. zip_hint is the whole sentence and {link} is where the link goes - put it where your language puts it; zip_link is the words inside that link.
groups.server.public.cache_: Public page: a big file on slow storage is copied locally before the download starts.
groups.server.public.folder_: Public page: a shared folder's file list.
groups.server.public.file_count: Public page: a shared folder's file list - the counts line "3 folders · 12 files".
groups.server.public.err_: Public page: a share link that cannot be served (title + one sentence).
groups.server.public.err_drop_: Public page: a file-request link that cannot be used (title + one sentence).
groups.server.public.drop_: Public page: the file-request (upload) page - a stranger uploads files into somebody's folder and cannot see its contents.
groups.server.public.drop_err_: Public page (file request): an upload the page refuses, or the server refused.
groups.server.public.drop_limit_: Public page (file request): the limits line under the drop zone, parts joined with " · ".
groups.server.public.footer: Public pages: the line at the bottom of every page. {filex} becomes the link to filex.sh - keep it exactly once.
groups.server.public.signing_in: The one-second page between single sign-on and the admin panel.
groups.server.public.continue: The one-second page between single sign-on and the admin panel: the link shown when the browser does not move on by itself.
The sentence under the sign-in form (and a WebDAV client's error) after a wrong password, or when too many wrong attempts have locked the account or the address. In the reader's language. Plain text; one or two sentences.
groups.server.login.wait_: A length of time inside a server.login.* sentence, slotted into {wait}: "3 minutes". Just the amount and its unit, no full stop.
API refusal when a page on another site sent a change (an upload, a delete, a sign-in) through the visitor's browser with their session, and filex refused it. Read mostly by whoever built that page, sometimes by the visitor. Keep `FILEX_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` exactly as written, between its backticks. Plain text; two sentences.
A notification - the bell, the browser's pop-up, the desktop app's, a push to a phone and its email - about one event. Composed by the SERVER in the reader's language from what happened, the same words on every one of them. Title: what happened, to what. Body: where, or the detail. Placeholders the event does not carry are removed together with the dash, arrow or colon next to them.
One line of a notification DIGEST - the single notification that tells a person, folder by folder, what changed while the kinds they did not mark urgent were held (one minute by default). Each is a count of one kind of change, joined after the folder name with commas: "Reports: 12 files added, 1 comment". Short, no full stop; the bell, the browser's pop-up, the desktop app and the digest email all say it.
A push notification the SERVER composes for a phone or a browser while filex is closed (Web Push) - the server's own words, sent in the reader's language. One short sentence.
A word a notification OR an email uses when the event does not say it (an upload with no name typed, a file with no name). One word, both surfaces - they were written twice until v0.43.0.
Admin panel (Users → Add / Edit) and the profile form: why an email address or a username was refused. Shown under the field it is about, in the reader's language. One sentence with a final full stop.
Admin panel (API / MCP) and a person's own API tokens: why the list of scopes (permissions) for a new token was refused. The scope names themselves (read, write, delete, mcp, admin, root:…) are typed by the person and stay in English.
Admin panel → Identity providers: why a change to a sign-in provider was refused, or the question asked before switching on a provider whose test failed.
groups.server.auth_provider.from_: Admin panel → Identity providers: where the environment defines a sign-in provider; used as {from} in server.auth_provider.environment_managed.
A notification administrators get when saved roles allow adding files (the Add files and folders permission) but not encrypting (the Encrypt permission): what a role saved on an older filex, which did not know Encrypt, is left with. Admin → Roles shows each with a button to give Encrypt back. Use the permission names as the role editor shows them (permissions.items.files.create.label and permissions.items.files.encrypt.label in the interface catalogue).
A notification a tenant's administrators get when the tenant's own domain (a CNAME to the tenant's address on the platform) stops pointing at it, so it stops working, or when it points there again.
Admin panel → Apps → an installed app's schedule: what the app's hourly wake-up amounted to, shown after the app's own summary, e.g. "nothing to do - 0 scheduled, 2 refused (…)". The parts are joined by server.list.separator.
The file manager, the admin panel, the command line: a rename, move, delete or save refused because an app (e.g. the signing app, while signatures are collected) holds the file. {app} starts the sentence; the app's own reason, when it gave one, ends it.
groups.server.list.separator: Between the items of a short list the server writes (e.g. an app's wake-up tally). A comma and a space in most languages; Arabic writes "، ".
Admin panel → Updates: why the newest release will (or will not) be installed by itself, shown under the version number. In the reader's language.
Admin panel → Updates: the name of an update policy (FILEX_UPDATE_POLICY), used as {policy} in server.update.reason.* sentences. Short, lower case.
Admin panel → External services (ONLYOFFICE, draw.io, the converter): why a service's settings were refused.
Admin panel → Storages (Add storage / edit a storage): why the storage's settings were refused. Shown as the error when saving. File and folder patterns (.git, *.tmp, downloads/incomplete/**) and the example folder names stay as written.
The trash, in the explorer's Trash view, the admin panel's Trash page and the answers an agent (MCP) gets: what a restore, a permanent delete or "Empty trash" did, and how much the trash holds. Short status lines and toasts.
groups.server.trash.clauses: Joins two parts of one trash notice: what went, then what did not and why ("2 items restored - 1 item could not be restored").
A line above the explorer's Trash: how many items it holds and how much space they take.
groups.server.trash.empty.confirm: The question in the "Empty the trash?" dialog, with the server's own count of what will be deleted. Shown before anything is deleted; the button under it deletes.
Where "Empty trash" stands: waiting, running (with progress), or how it ended. A toast and a status line in the explorer and the admin panel.
A toast after Restore in the Trash (one item or a selection), or the operations centre's line for a restore job.
A toast after "Delete permanently" in the Trash, or the operations centre's line for that job.
A unit after a size - in emails (the size of a shared file) and on the no-JavaScript folder page: "1,5 MB". The same units the interface writes (the unit.* keys); a language that writes "Mo" or "Go" there writes them here too.
The bell of the people who edited a document in ONLYOFFICE, when the document server's save was written beside the file (in another format) or not written at all. A title, and one or two sentences under it.
An answer that does not fit the field that asked for it, on a form an app draws (a screen in the file manager, an app's public page, an app's settings in the admin panel): shown under the field, or once for the whole form. One short instruction to the person filling it in.
groups.server.share.pin_length: Share dialog: refusal when a link's PIN is shorter or longer than allowed. One sentence.
Admin panel → Audit log, and the dashboard's Recent activity: the words a row is said in - what happened (its action) and what it happened to (its target).
Audit log: the kind of thing an action changed, a short noun with a capital letter (User, Storage, Share), used as {resource} in server.audit.phrase (“User: deleted”) and as the thing's kind where server.audit.target.* has no word of its own. A word ending in “(AI)” is the same thing changed by an AI agent.
Audit log: what was done to the thing, a short lower-case past participle or noun phrase (deleted, password reset), used as {verb} in server.audit.phrase (“User: deleted”).
Audit log: the kind of thing a row is about, a short noun with a capital letter (User, File), used as {kind} in server.audit.target_named (“User “ada@example.com””) and server.audit.target_numbered (“Share #12”).
groups.server.update.policy_is: Admin panel → Updates: the badge that names the saved update policy.
Admin panel → Updates: the badge that says what filex really does on this install, shown instead of the policy's name when the saved policy cannot take effect here (update checks off, a container, a package manager). Two or three words.
Admin panel → Updates: why the saved update policy has no effect (or only part of it) on this install, shown under the policy. One or two sentences; {policy} stands in quotes.
Admin panel → Webhooks: refusal when a webhook's settings are saved, shown under the field it is about. One sentence.
Admin panel → Notifications, the history table's Webhook column: why a notification was not sent to the webhooks (the row is marked skipped). One sentence.
Admin panel → Protection: refusal of a number typed into one of its limits, shown under the field. One sentence.
Admin panel → Usage & cost: a note under the storage provider's report about where its numbers come from. One sentence.
Admin panel → Identity providers, Test: one line per step of the provider's test (reached, signed in, found), ✓ or ✗ beside it. One sentence; a failed step ends with why, a server.auth_provider.reason.* phrase.
Admin panel → Identity providers, Test: why a step failed, a lower-case phrase slotted into a server.auth_provider.check.* sentence as {reason}.

keys.server.update.policy.manual: The stored value of the update policy setting (FILEX_UPDATE_POLICY=manual) said the way a person reads it - filex announces a release and installs nothing. Translate the MEANING ("announce only"), not the key’s word "manual".
keys.server.notify.word.locked: Stands in the bell for the name of an item inside an end-to-end encrypted folder whose names are encrypted, while the reader does not have that folder unlocked - the server only has the scrambled name. Keep the lock emoji; it matches the explorer’s own label for such an item.
keys.server.notify.word.someone: Used where a person would be named and nobody is: the {who} of an upload whose visitor typed no name - in the bell AND in the owner’s email.
keys.server.notify.word.unnamed: Used where a file would be named and it has none: the {name} of a notification, and the {name} in a share email’s subject and fact line.
keys.server.notify.e2e.request_decided.title_: The same notification when an administrator said no; the title without the suffix is the yes.
keys.server.mail.drop_invite.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.grant.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.account.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.drop_received.subject: Subject line, and the notification's stored title.
keys.server.mail.smtp_test.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.cloud_verify.subject: Subject line.
keys.server.mail.cloud_verify.how: {ttl} is written by the server as a duration such as 24h0m0s.
keys.server.public.folder_title_suffix: After the folder's name in the browser tab: "Photos - shared folder".
keys.server.public.pin_aria: Read aloud by screen readers for the PIN box.
keys.server.public.drop_zone_aria: Read aloud by screen readers for the drop zone.
keys.server.public.drop_remove_aria: Read aloud by screen readers for the ✕ beside a picked file.
keys.server.public.drop_name_ph: Example text inside the empty name box - use a typical name of the language.
keys.server.notify.plugin.notice.body: An installed app's own notification: "<app name>: <the app's message>".
keys.server.audit.phrase: The action of a row: {resource} is the kind of thing (a server.audit.resource.* word), {verb} what was done (a server.audit.verb.* word). Keep the colon form unless your language needs another order.
keys.server.audit.via_ai: A kind of thing changed by an AI agent rather than a person, e.g. “File (AI)”.
keys.server.audit.target_named: What a row is about, by name: {kind} is a server.audit.target.* or server.audit.resource.* word, {name} the thing's name as stored.
keys.server.audit.target_numbered: What a row is about when it has only a number: {kind} as in target_named, {id} the number.
keys.server.audit.hidden_address: On a public demo the visitors' IP addresses are masked in the audit log; this is said in place of the masked address. Lower case: it stands where an address would.

vars.ext: a file extension without the dot, e.g. exe
vars.action: what the person tried to do - one of the server.perm.action.* phrases
vars.rule: the name an administrator gave a role (a custom role; the key keeps its older name)
vars.group: the name an administrator gave a group of people (Admin → Groups)
vars.name: a file or folder name, as it is on disk
vars.link: a clickable link, already made - put it where your language puts it; the words inside it are their own key
vars.done: how many items have been dealt with so far (a number)
vars.total: how many items there are in all (a number)
vars.first: the first part of the notice, a whole sentence in this language
vars.second: the second part of the notice, a whole sentence in this language
vars.wait: a length of time with its unit, e.g. 3 minutes
vars.date: a date and time in the reader's time zone, e.g. 2026-10-03 14:00 (or 2026-10-03 14:00 UTC when the account has no time zone)
vars.max: a whole number, the most items one request may name, e.g. 200
vars.site: the site name the administrator set (Settings → Branding)
vars.size: a size with its unit, e.g. 1.4 MB
vars.types: file extensions, comma-separated, e.g. pdf, jpg
vars.who: the uploader's name as they typed it, or the word for "someone"
vars.submission: the name of the new sub-folder the upload was put in, e.g. 2026-09-22_101500_Ana
vars.item: the storage and path of the item, e.g. Files://Reports/2026
vars.url: the address of the sign-in page
vars.email: the email address of the new account
vars.ttl: how long the token lasts, e.g. 24h0m0s
vars.app: the installed app's name, e.g. Signatures
vars.host: an internet host name, e.g. api.example.com
vars.engine: a conversion program's name, e.g. ffmpeg
vars.filex: the word filex as a link to filex.sh - keep it exactly once
vars.path: the file's path inside its storage, e.g. /Reports/2026/q3.pdf
vars.reason: the storage's own error message, in English
vars.signature: the virus scanner's name for what it found
vars.from: the path the item was at
vars.to: the path the item is at now
vars.pamtester: the full path of the pamtester program on the server, e.g. /usr/bin/pamtester (a path, written the same in every language)
vars.sudo: the full path of the sudo program on the server, e.g. /usr/bin/sudo
vars.service: the PAM service name (a file in /etc/pam.d), e.g. filex
vars.pamfile: the full path of the PAM service file, e.g. /etc/pam.d/filex
vars.runas: the operating-system account filex runs as, e.g. filex
vars.uploader: the uploader's name as they typed it, or the word for "someone"
vars.body: the first 200 characters of the comment
vars.notice_title: the installed app's own title for its notification
vars.notice_body: the installed app's own text for its notification
vars.op: the replica operation that failed (write, delete, move)
vars.scope: a scope (permission) name exactly as the person typed it
vars.char: the one character that is not allowed, e.g. ş
vars.policy: the update policy's name, one of the server.update.policy.* words
vars.saved: the name the edit was saved under, beside the file, e.g. report.docx
vars.format: a file format's name in capitals, e.g. DOCX
vars.why: one sentence that says why a save was not written (one of the server.onlyoffice.refused_* sentences, already in the reader's language)

server.sync.progress.listing_here_one.here: how many items were found on this computer (a number)

server.sync.progress.transfer.done: how many files have been moved so far (a number)
server.sync.progress.transfer.total: how many files this pass moves (a number)

server.sync.progress.transfer_bytes.done: how many files have been moved so far (a number)
server.sync.progress.transfer_bytes.total: how many files this pass moves (a number)
server.sync.progress.transfer_bytes.bytes: the size moved so far, with its unit, e.g. 1.2 GB

server.sync.progress.transfer_eta.done: how many files have been moved so far (a number)
server.sync.progress.transfer_eta.total: how many files this pass moves (a number)
server.sync.progress.transfer_eta.bytes: the size moved so far, with its unit, e.g. 1.2 GB

server.sync.progress.settling.done: how many changes have been recorded (a number)
server.sync.progress.settling.total: how many changes there are to record (a number)

server.sync.pass.done.done: how many of the changes were made (a number)

server.sync.pass.done_failed_one.failed: how many of them could not be made (a number)

server.sync.pass.action_failed.error: the item and why, in the engine's own words (English)

server.sync.pass.raced.name: the item and what was being done to it, in the engine's own words (English)

server.sync.pass.skipped.name: the path of one skipped item, inside the synced folder

server.sync.pass.skipped_one.name: the path of the skipped item, inside the synced folder

server.sync.lock.failed.error: why, in the operating system's own words (English)

server.sync.local.too_large.seconds: the interval of the safety-net check, in seconds, e.g. 30

server.sync.local.unavailable.seconds: the interval of the safety-net check, in seconds, e.g. 30

server.sync.live.polling.seconds: the interval of the safety-net check, in seconds, e.g. 30

server.sync.live.off.seconds: the interval of the safety-net check, in seconds, e.g. 30

server.sync.window.waiting.window: the hours syncing is allowed in, local time, e.g. 22:00-07:00

server.sync.window.closed.window: the hours syncing is allowed in, local time, e.g. 22:00-07:00

server.sync.pairs_unreadable.error: why, in the engine's own words (English)

server.sync.fatal.error: why, in the engine's own words (English)

server.e2e.vault.locked.name: the display name of the person whose session holds the vault's write lock, e.g. Ayşe Yılmaz

server.e2e.vault.generation.latest: the number of the vault's newest generation (an integer, counting its commits), e.g. 12
